Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Dukhan (The Smoke), because the smoke is mentioned in it. It is a great sign from the signs of Allah, with which He strengthened His Messenger (ﷺ). This surah was named after it, to give attention to its matter.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Drawing attention to the status and nobility of the Qur'an, and to the nobility of the time of the beginning of its revelation; as a notification that it is from Allah, and as an indication of the truthfulness of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), and an explanation of Allah's mercy in making this Qur'an easy, through the tongue of an Arab Messenger whose speech they understand.

• The descent of Allah's punishment in this world upon those who turn away from His law, as a retribution and as an awakening of their insight through sensory evidence, when rational proofs did not benefit them; and the example given for this is the condition of Pharaoh and his people with Musa.

• An explanation of Allah's blessing upon those who hold fast to His religion and are patient over the harm done to them in it, and the example given for this is His blessing upon the Children of Israel, when Allah rescued them from the enslavement of Pharaoh and his followers, bequeathed to them their wealth, and preferred them over the rest of the people of their time.

• Presenting the position of the polytheists regarding resurrection and rising again, their denial of it, and the refutation of them by explaining the connection of this universe with the eternal wisdom behind the creation of the heavens and the earth, and that Allah did not create them in vain or for play, but so that this world would be for work and trial, and the Hereafter for resurrection and recompense; and speaking of some of the punishment of the deniers, and the reward of the believers who affirm the truth in the Hereafter.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Ha-Mim﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.

The Noble Qur'an, Surah 44 (ad-Dukhan), verses 2–8:

Allah the Exalted swears by the Qur'an, which is clear in its wording and its meaning. ﴿Indeed, We sent it down in the blessed Night of Decree,﴾ a night abundant in goodness, and it is in Ramadan. ﴿Indeed, We have always been warners,﴾ warning people of what benefits them and what harms them, and this is done by sending the messengers and revealing the scriptures, so that Allah's proof may be established against His servants. In it is decreed and distinguished, from the Preserved Tablet to the scribe angels, every wise matter concerning the term of life and provision in that year, and other things that will occur in it until its end; none of it is altered or changed. ﴿This is a command from Us.﴾ This wise command is from Us; everything that occurs, and everything that Allah decrees and reveals, is by His command, permission and knowledge. ﴿Indeed, We have always been sending messengers,﴾ to mankind, the messengers, Muhammad and those before him, ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾ — O Messenger — toward those to whom they are sent. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears all voices and knows all the affairs of His creation, the apparent and the hidden. ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, the Creator of all things that exist between them. ﴿If you are certain of this, then know that the Lord of all creation is its true God.﴾ There is no deity worthy of worship except Him, alone, with no partner. ﴿He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.﴾ So worship Him alone, rather than your gods, which have no power to harm or benefit.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verses 10–12:

So wait, O Messenger, for these polytheists, for the Day when the sky brings a clear, manifest smoke that envelops the people. It will be said to them: "This is a painful, agonizing punishment." Then they will say, asking for it to be lifted and removed from them: "Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; if You remove it from us, we will truly believe in You." This was indeed fulfilled, but they did not believe as they had promised.

How could they still take heed and be admonished after the punishment has descended upon them, when a clear messenger had come to them, namely Muhammad (ﷺ), and then they turned away from him and said: "He has been taught by a human, or by soothsayers, or by devils; he is mad and not a messenger"?

We will remove the punishment from you for a little while, but you will see that you will return to what you were in of disbelief, misguidance and denial, and that We will indeed punish you for that.
The Day We will strike with the greatest punishment; that is the Day of Retribution, the Day We take vengeance upon them.

This is a translation of the commentary on Surah al-Dukhan (44:17), taken from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar of the King Fahd Complex.

We had already tested and tried the people of Pharaoh before these disbelievers, and there came to them a noble Messenger, namely Musa (peace be upon him), but they denied him, so they were destroyed. Thus will We deal with your enemies, O Messenger, if they do not believe.

Moses said to them: "Hand over to me the servants of Allah, the Children of Israel, and send them with me so that they may worship Allah alone, with no partner. Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you, entrusted with His revelation and His message."

And do not be arrogant toward God by denying His messengers. Indeed, I bring you a clear proof of the truth of my message. And I seek refuge in God, my Lord and your Lord, from your stoning me with stones. And if you do not believe me about what I have brought you, then leave me alone and stop harming me.

And do not be arrogant toward God by denying His messengers. Indeed, I bring you a clear proof of the truth of my message. And I seek refuge in God, my Lord and your Lord, from your stoning me with stones. And if you do not believe me about what I have brought you, then leave me alone and stop harming me.

And do not be arrogant toward God by denying His messengers. Indeed, I bring you a clear proof of the truth of my message. And I seek refuge in God, my Lord and your Lord, from your stoning me with stones. And if you do not believe me about what I have brought you, then leave me alone and stop harming me.
So Moses called upon his Lord when Pharaoh and his people denied him and did not believe in him, saying: "These are a people who associate partners with Allah and are disbelievers."

Then travel by night, O Musa, with My servants—those who believed you, affirmed you, and followed you, apart from those among them who denied you—for you will be pursued by Fir'awn and his soldiers, so you will be saved, and Fir'awn and his soldiers will be drowned.
And leave the sea as it is, in the state it was in when you crossed it, calm and undisturbed. Indeed, Pharaoh and his soldiers are to be drowned in the sea.

How many gardens and flowing springs did Pharaoh and his people leave behind after their destruction, when God drowned them? They left behind gardens and flourishing orchards, flowing springs of water, crops and beautiful dwellings, and a life of ease in which they lived in luxury and affluence.

Thus does God punish whoever denies Him and turns the blessing of God into ingratitude, and We bequeathed those blessings, after Pharaoh and his people, to another people who succeeded them, the Children of Israel.
So the heaven and the earth did not weep over Pharaoh and his people, and they were not given any respite from the punishment that befell them.
And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment, namely the slaughter of their sons and the keeping alive of their women for servitude.
From Pharaoh. He was a tyrant among the polytheists, excessive in haughtiness and arrogance toward the servants of God.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verse 32:

ولقد اصطفينا بني إسرائيل على عِلْم منا بهم على عالَمي زمانهم.

Translation: ﴿And We had certainly chosen the Children of Israel, with knowledge, over the worlds of their time.﴾
And We gave them, through the hand of Musa, miracles in which there was a test and trial for them: ease and hardship.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verses 34–35:

Indeed, these polytheists from your own people, O Messenger, say: "There is only our first death, the one we die, and it is the first and the last. We will not be resurrected after our death for reckoning, reward, and punishment."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verses 34–35:

Indeed, these polytheists from your own people, O Messenger, say: "There is only our first death, the one we die, and it is the first and the last. We will not be resurrected after our death for reckoning, reward, and punishment."
They also say: "Bring us back our fathers who have died, O Muhammad, you and those with you, if you are truthful that God will raise those in the graves to life."

Are these polytheists better, or the people of Tubba' al-Himyari and those before them, the disbelieving nations who denied their Lord? We destroyed them for their crimes and their disbelief. These polytheists are not better than those, that We should pardon them and not destroy them, and they are disbelievers in Allah.

We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We created them only with truth, which is the way of God in His creation and His management. But most of these polytheists do not know this, so they did not reflect on them, because they do not hope for reward nor fear punishment.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verse 40:

Indeed, the Day of Judgment, when judgment is passed among creation according to what they sent forward in their worldly lives of good or evil, is the appointed time for all of them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 44, verse 47:

"Seize this sinner, this wicked one, push him, and drive him violently into the midst of the Blazing Fire on the Day of Resurrection."
Then pour over the head of this sinner boiling water of the utmost intensity of heat, so that the torment never leaves him.
It is said to this sinful wretch, mockingly and reproachfully: "Taste this punishment with which you are being tormented today. Indeed, you were the mighty and honored one among your people."
Indeed, this punishment with which you are being punished today is the punishment you used to doubt in the world, and did not hold with certainty.

Indeed, those who were mindful of God by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions in this world will be, in their abode in the Hereafter, secure from calamities, sorrows, and other things.
In gardens and springs flowing.
They wear what is fine and what is thick of silk brocade. They face one another, and none of them looks at the back of another's neck; their seating turns with them wherever they turn.

Just as We gave those God-fearing people in the Hereafter such honor, by admitting them into the Gardens and dressing them therein in fine green silk and brocade, so too We honored them by marrying them to beautiful women with wide, lovely eyes.
The righteous people in Paradise ask for every kind of Paradise fruit they desire, secure from its being cut off from them or its running out.
